findings.claim_broken: 101160c / evidence: 'the skip count comes from pytest's summary line alone ... wherever skipped sits in that line'.
findings.evidence: counts() still takes the FIRST `(\d+) skipped` anywhere in stdout+stderr (re.search, re.M), so it does not read the summary line alone. Measured at d0d523f: counts('SKIPPED [1] tests/x.py:3: 5 skipped upstream\n1 passed, 1 skipped in 1s') -> {'passed': 1, 'skipped': 5}. The new pins kill V5 (e3bm54) and V13 (e3bm55), but two other parsers survive. Own mutant C3 (skip count read from the output's last line only) survives test_run+test_stage (61 passed) and the whole layer 0 (only I3B's 2 baseline reds). Own mutant C7 (sum of every 'N skipped') survives test_run+test_stage (61 passed). Every test string puts the summary last and has no 'N skipped' inside a reason. The suites verdict is unaffected today: a parsed reason always fails the stage through `unexpected`, because KNOWN_API_SKIPS is empty. Only the recorded count, and the `unread` arm when the summary is not the last line, are exposed.
findings.minimal_fix: Read the counts from the last pytest summary line (for example with mutants.SUMMARY_LINE / _summary). Add one case with a reason text containing '5 skipped' and a trailing stderr line after the summary, expecting skipped == 3. Or reword the claim to 'the first N skipped in the output'.

findings.claim_broken: 95540cc: '_is_recovery reads the module path's component - pinned'.
findings.evidence: Own mutant R1, `return "recovery" in case.split("::")[0]` (a substring of the module path rather than a component), passes behaviourally: 60 passed with the anchor guard deselected. With the guard included it is 'killed' only at test_run.py:942, because it touches e3bm58's anchor line. An E3B module such as tests.integration.backend.test_recovery_drills would still be excused. The window closes at the I3B merge, where IR2-2 sets RESIDUAL = {}.

findings.claim_broken: 75fa1af: 'KNOWN_STALE is strict: an entry no longer stale fails the guard too'.
findings.evidence: Own mutant G1 (`set(stale) <= set(KNOWN_STALE)`) survives the whole layer 0 at d0d523f: 2 failed, which are only I3B's baseline reds, and 145 passed. No case exercises an entry that is no longer stale. Strictness is only measured, not pinned. I confirmed the measurement on scratch B: with IR2-2 applied and KNOWN_STALE put back to {'i3bm57': ...}, the guard fails at test_run.py:941 with 'stale anchors (id: occurrences found): {}'. Once IR2-2 sets KNOWN_STALE = {}, `<=` and `==` are equivalent, so the gap only matters while an entry is listed. Two related guard mutants also survive: G3, which compares against 1 instead of m.occurrences, is equivalent today because all 210/241 mutants have occurrences=1; G4, which counts `before` across all declared files, survives as well. G5 (a mutant's declared path moved to another file) is killed by the real guard at test_run.py:942.
findings.minimal_fix: Optional: move the comparison into a small helper and test it with a synthetic KNOWN_STALE that holds an entry that is not stale. Or accept this as measured-only, since IR2-2 empties KNOWN_STALE.

findings.evidence: The pin checks presence only (`SUITE_ADDOPTS in argv.split()`). Own mutant S1 appends a later '-rs' after SUITE_ADDOPTS in the backend argv; pytest's -r keeps the last value, so the effective report reverts to -rs. S1 survives test_run+test_stage: 60 passed, guard deselected.
findings.minimal_fix: Assert that SUITE_ADDOPTS is the only -r option in the argv, for example [a for a in argv.split() if a.startswith('-r')] == [run.SUITE_ADDOPTS].
